summary: A bijou region packed with distinctive wines...
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Richard Baudains was born and bred in Jersey in the Channel Islands and trained to be a teacher of English as a foreign language. After several years in various foreign climes, Baudains settled down in beautiful Friuli-Venezia Giulia, having had the good fortune to reside previously in the winemaking regions of Piemonte, Tuscany, Liguria and Trentino-Alto Adige. Baudains wrote his first article for <em>Decanter</em> in 1989 and has been a regular contributor on Italian wines ever since. His day job as director of a language school conveniently leaves time for a range of wine-related activities including writing for the <em>Slow</em> wine guide, leading tastings and lecturing in wine journalism at L’Università degli Studi di Scienze Gastronomiche and for the web-based Wine Scholars’ Guild.</p></div>

title: Expert's Choice: 18 scintillating South American sparkling wines
content: <p>Amanda Barnes is an award-winning wine journalist and expert in South American wines and regions. </p><p>Based in Mendoza since 2009 she is a regular South America correspondent, critic and writer for <em>Decanter</em>, as well as other international wine publications, and she is the author and editor of the <em>South America Wine Guide</em>. </p><p>She has been awarded by Born Digital Wine Awards, Millesima Blog Awards, Great Wine Capitals Best Of and Young Wine Writer of the Year. </p><p>She has received a fellowship from the Wine Writers Symposium, a scholarship for the Wine Bloggers Conference, and the Geoffrey Roberts Award. </p>

title: The smart buyer's guide to... Malbec
content: <div class="author-description"><p><span style="font-weight: 400">Ines is Decanter’s regional editor for Spain, Portugal and South America. Born and raised in Lisbon, Portugal, she grew up chasing her grandfather among his vines in Ribatejo and thus her love for all things wine began. After completing her Masters Degree in Architecture, Ines worked as a project manager while writing about wine and doing cellar consulting on the side. After moving to London in 2015, she decided to dedicate herself fully to the wine industry and joined the sommelier team at Michelin-starred Spring, Somerset House. Stints at Noble Rot and The Laughing Heart followed, while completing her WSET Diploma in Wines and Spirits. Her work as a judge and writer eventually became her full time commitment and she joined Decanter in 2019 as wine database editor. </span></p></div>

title: The beauty of balance: Get to know equal-parts cocktails
summary: Mixing a drink in exactly equal measures is one of the easiest ways to make a cocktail. But what makes these even ratio drinks so delicious – and enduring? Alicia Miller speaks to top bartenders to find out, with recipes to try at home.
content: <div class="author-description"><p>A former editor at The Sunday Times, Alicia Miller has more than a dozen years of experience writing about drink, food and travel. She is WSET Level 3-accredited and was named 2022's Travel Writer of the Year by AITO. Her work has taken her to more than 50 countries.</p></div>

title: Boisset acquires Artesa as California wine history repeats itself
summary: Jean-Charles Boisset makes a significant investment in Carneros amid falling wine consumption
content: <p>Jonathan Cristaldi is a wine writer and critic based in the San Francisco Bay Area. For more than a decade, his articles on wine, spirits and beer have appeared in a host of print and digital platforms, including Decanter, Food &amp; Wine, Departures, The SOMM Journal, Tasting Panel Magazine, Liquor.com, Seven Fifty Daily, Los Angeles Magazine, Thrillist, Tasting Table and <em>Time Out LA </em>among others. When not writing about wine, Cristaldi works as a scriptwriter on film and documentary projects with award-winning commercial photographer and director Rachid Dahnoun.</p>

summary: Still a buyer's market out there...
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Chris Mercer is a Bristol-based freelance editor and journalist who spent nearly four years as digital editor of <strong>Decanter.com</strong>, having previously been <em>Decanter’s</em> news editor across online and print.</p><p>He has written about, and reported on, the wine and food sectors for more than 10 years for both consumer and trade media.</p><p>Chris first became interested in the wine world while living in Languedoc-Roussillon after completing a journalism Masters in the UK. These days, his love of wine commonly tests his budgeting skills.</p><p>Beyond wine, Chris also has an MSc in food policy and has a particular interest in sustainability issues. He has also been a food judge at the UK’s Great Taste Awards.</p></div>
